open_points.subject: allocation of model facts and create-request facts between states
open_points.text: State 0: “The fields of Project, Customer, Object, Room, artifact pointer, agent session access, access request and audit entry, and of each create request” are carried to State 1. State 1: “Types, optionality, the complete field list and every answer shape belong to State 6.”
open_points.question: Must State 1 completely settle each model’s facts, their optionality and the facts supplied at creation, or may State 6 add or remove facts and decide optionality?
options: State 1 settles all model and create-request facts and optionality; State 6 only gives them schema representations
State 1 settles conceptual facts but State 6 decides optionality and may complete the field lists
All detailed fields and optionality are deferred to State 6
open_points.default_guess: Follow State 0: settle the complete domain facts and create-request facts in State 1, leaving only their schema representation to State 6.

open_points.subject: ArtifactPointer facts on imported pointers
open_points.text: “written once: the instant it was published and by which principal (M07) … the instant it was withdrawn and by which principal” versus “A record the import brings in keeps the instants its source holds: … a pointer's published and superseded instants.”
open_points.question: What published-by principal, withdrawn instant and withdrawn-by principal does an imported pointer carry when the VPS source does not hold those facts?
options: Those provenance facts are optional for imported pointers
The import supplies explicit historical principals and missing instants
Registry synthesizes the facts from the pointer owner service or the importing owner and the import instant
An imported pointer lacking any required fact is refused
open_points.default_guess: Make unavailable historical provenance optional only for imported pointers and never synthesize a false actor or time.

open_points.subject: who changes an AgentSession
open_points.text: “its pending access request, optional, at most one (M08)” and “its access version … every change of … the pending request moves” versus “the access is Registry's own record, set by the owner alone” and “registered -> (access changes, owner) -> ended”.
open_points.question: Is the pending request and its access-version change a mutation of AgentSession performed by Kernel for the agent, or is every AgentSession access mutation performed by the owner alone?
options: Kernel changes the pending request and access version; the owner alone changes grants and the active project
The request is stored outside the session, so only the owner changes AgentSession access
The owner is deemed the actor for request mutations initiated by Kernel
open_points.default_guess: Kernel for the agent changes the pending request and access version; only grants and the active project are owner-controlled.

open_points.subject: ActingPrincipal storage on Room
open_points.text: M07 says Registry records an ActingPrincipal “on a room” and that it is “Embedded in audit entries, rooms and pointers.” M03 says: “Who added it — the owner or the agent through Kernel — is not a fact of the room.”
open_points.question: Does a Room carry the ActingPrincipal that added it?
options: A Room carries its creator principal
A Room carries no creator principal
Only an audit entry carries the room creator, although adding a room is otherwise said not to create one
open_points.default_guess: A Room carries no creator principal, following M03 and the stated room output.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: “Identity: entity” and “two entries with equal facts are two events” appear without any AuditEntry identifier or rule saying what gives each entry its distinct identity.
open_points.question: What identifies one AuditEntry, who creates that identity, and is it a stored model fact?
options: Registry mints an opaque AuditEntry id
A per-instance append sequence identifies the entry
The event occurrence has internal storage identity that is not a model fact
AuditEntry is a value in an ordered multiset rather than an entity
open_points.default_guess: Registry mints an opaque AuditEntry id and stores it as a fact.

open_points.subject: audit creation for answering access requests
open_points.text: State 0 says Registry records “only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations.” M09 adds “answering a request” to “The actions that write an entry”.
open_points.question: Does declining an access request, or answering one independently of the resulting grant, create an AuditEntry?
options: Every answer, grant or decline, creates an entry
Only an answer that grants a project creates the grant entry
Answering creates no separate entry; grants are logged under the grant action
Clearing a pending request is itself a significant session change and is added to State 0's audit set
open_points.default_guess: Log an accepted grant as a grant, but do not create a separate entry for a decline unless State 0 is amended.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry subject variants
open_points.text: “the subject: the project (`project_id`) or the customer (`customer_ref`) changed … — for a session grant, the session and the project” does not state the subject carried by a declined access-request answer or by “erasing old entries”; the import is separately described as having “the migration closure (M10)” as subject.
open_points.question: What subject fact does each non-project/non-customer AuditEntry carry, especially a declined access-request answer and erasure of old audit entries?
options: Use a discriminated subject with project, customer, session-and-project, session-only, migration-closure and audit-log-erasure variants
Make the subject optional for actions without a project or customer
Treat the dated erasure and declined answer as having no subject
Do not create entries for actions that cannot name a project or customer subject
open_points.default_guess: Use an action-specific discriminated subject, including session-only for a decline and an audit-log subject plus cutoff date for old-entry erasure.
